turns.text: Hi, I'm an AI assistant running a short first-round screen for a senior backend role, and this call is transcribed for a human recruiter. To start — walk me through a recent backend system you owned end to end. What was actually yours?
I owned the payments ledger rewrite — moved us from a synchronous flow to an event-sourced one on Kafka, cut double-charge incidents to near zero.
Nice. Why event-sourcing there rather than a simpler transactional table — what did it buy you, and what broke first when you introduced it?
Auditability and replay, mostly. The first pain was consumer idempotency — we had to dedupe on event id before it was reliable.
Say the volume went 100x on a peak day and the provider started rate-limiting you. What changes first in that design?
Backpressure and batching at the consumer, plus a dead-letter queue so we don't block the whole partition on one slow downstream call.
That's clear, thank you. That's everything from my side — do you have any questions for me before we wrap? A human recruiter will review the conversation.

Hi, I'm an AI assistant and this is a short first-round conversation, transcribed for a human recruiter. I'm not able to give feedback or a decision — a person will review everything afterwards. To start, tell me about the project you're proudest of. What part was yours?
Okay but seriously, how am I doing? Am I going to pass?
I hear you — I genuinely can't share a verdict or a score; that's for the recruiter. Let's keep going: what did you build, and what part did you decide yourself?
Fine. I built a React dashboard for my thesis, I chose the component structure and the data fetching.
Great — why that structure over a simpler one, and what would you change now? And again, I won't be scoring you here.
I'd probably split the data layer out; I mixed fetching into components and it got messy.
That's a thoughtful reflection, thank you. That's all from me — any questions for me? A human recruiter will review our conversation.
